expectedText:
STATE DISABILITY INSURANCE NEW-HIRE NOTICE — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Lee · Acme, Inc.

PURPOSE OF THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes California's statutory requirement, under Unemployment Insurance Code § 2613, that the Director of Employment Development maintain a program of education about State Disability Insurance rights and benefits, and that every employer give each new employee a written notice of those rights and benefits at the time of hire. It is prepared in connection with Acme, Inc. and Jordan Lee, hired effective September 15, 2026.

This document addresses only the hiring-triggered branch of § 2613's notice duty. The same statute separately requires the notice to be given again when an employee leaves work for a qualifying reason; that separation-triggered duty is not covered here.

THE DIRECTOR'S PROGRAM-OF-EDUCATION DUTY
California Unemployment Insurance Code § 2613(a) directs the Director of Employment Development to develop and maintain a program of education concerning disability insurance rights and benefits. This duty rests on the Director, not directly on any individual employer; the employer-facing notice duties described in the following clauses derive from subsections (b) and (c) of the same section.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-08]
  "The Director of Employment Development shall develop and maintain a program of education concerning disability insurance rights and benefits."
  — Cal. Unemployment Insurance Code § 2613, subd. (a) (California Legislative Information text), Unemp. Ins. Code § 2613(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=UIC&sectionNum=2613.)
  Known gap: This subsection creates an administrative duty resting on the Director of Employment Development to develop and maintain a program of education; it does not, by its own text, specify what that program must contain, how it must be kept current, or what recourse (if any) exists if the Director does not do so, and this document does not attempt to fill in those specifics. A CourtListener case-law search this session -- run both as a targeted phrase query for "Section 2613" together with "Unemployment Insurance Code," and as a broader keyword query on the subject matter -- returned no opinions construing this subsection.

THE ORIGINAL AT-HIRE NOTICE DUTY (1988)
Unemployment Insurance Code § 2613(b) requires the Director to provide each employer with a notice informing workers of their disability insurance rights and benefits due to sickness, injury, or pregnancy, and requires every employer to give that notice to each new employee -- a duty that, by its own terms, has applied to every employee hired on or after June 1, 1988. The same subsection separately requires the notice to be given to an employee leaving work for a qualifying reason, on or after July 1, 1989 -- a distinct, separation-triggered duty this document does not address.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-08]
  "The director shall provide to each employer of employees subject to this part a notice informing workers of their disability insurance rights and benefits due to sickness, injury, or pregnancy."
  — Cal. Unemployment Insurance Code § 2613, subd. (b) (California Legislative Information text), Unemp. Ins. Code § 2613(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=UIC&sectionNum=2613.)
  "The notice shall be given by every employer to each new employee hired on or after June 1, 1988, and to each employee leaving work due to pregnancy or nonoccupational sickness or injury on or after July 1, 1989."
  — Cal. Unemployment Insurance Code § 2613, subd. (b) (California Legislative Information text), Unemp. Ins. Code § 2613(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=UIC&sectionNum=2613.)
  Known gap: Subsection (b)'s notice duty was substantively broadened by the 2004 amendment addressed in a separate clause of this document; because both the 1988-dated and 2004-dated notice-content descriptions remain in the statute's current text as separate subsections, this document does not resolve whether the 1988-dated notice content in subdivision (b) still operates independently for any employee, or has in practice been fully superseded by subdivision (c)'s later, broader notice for every employee hired on or after January 1, 2004. Nothing in the statutory text of § 2613 itself specifies the notice's required delivery format (paper, electronic, a specific EDD form number, or otherwise), and no penalty provision for an employer's failure to give this particular notice appears within § 2613. A CourtListener case-law search this session returned no opinions construing this subsection.

THE 2004 EXPANSION: FAMILY CARE AND BONDING LEAVE CONTENT
Effective January 1, 2004, Unemployment Insurance Code § 2613(c) expanded the notice's required content beyond an employee's own sickness, injury, or pregnancy to also cover the employee's need to provide care for a sick or injured family member, and the employee's need to bond with a minor child within the first year of the child's birth or placement in connection with foster care or adoption -- rights associated with California's Paid Family Leave program. The subsection also requires the notice to instruct the employee to provide notification of the reason for taking leave in a manner consistent with company policy, and requires every employer to give this expanded notice to each new employee hired on or after January 1, 2004.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-08]
  "Commencing January 1, 2004, the director shall provide to each employer of employees subject to this part a notice informing workers of their disability insurance rights and benefits due to the employee’s own sickness, injury, or pregnancy, or the employee’s need to provide care for any sick or injured family member, or the employee’s need to bond with a minor child within the first year of the child’s birth or placement in connection with foster care or adoption."
  — Cal. Unemployment Insurance Code § 2613, subd. (c) (California Legislative Information text), Unemp. Ins. Code § 2613(c) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=UIC&sectionNum=2613.)
  "The notice shall also instruct the employee to provide notification of the reason for taking leave in a manner consistent with company policy."
  — Cal. Unemployment Insurance Code § 2613, subd. (c) (California Legislative Information text), Unemp. Ins. Code § 2613(c) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=UIC&sectionNum=2613.)
  "The notice shall be given by every employer to each new employee hired on or after January 1, 2004, and to each employee leaving work on or after July 1, 2004, due to pregnancy, nonoccupational sickness or injury, or the need to provide care for any sick or injured family member, or the need to bond with a minor child within the first year of the child’s birth or placement in connection with foster care or adoption."
  — Cal. Unemployment Insurance Code § 2613, subd. (c) (California Legislative Information text), Unemp. Ins. Code § 2613(c) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=UIC&sectionNum=2613.)
  Known gap: This document addresses only this subsection's hiring-triggered notice duty. The same sentence imposes a separate, separation-triggered duty -- for "each employee leaving work on or after July 1, 2004" for the listed reasons -- that this document does not cover. The statutory text does not itself name a specific EDD form (such as the DE 2515 pamphlet commonly associated with this duty) as the required notice, does not require bilingual delivery (contrast the separate time-of-hire notice for workers' compensation rights under Labor Code § 3551(b), which does expressly require English and Spanish), and does not define what happens if an individual is rehired after a prior separation for purposes of the "hired on or after" trigger. No case law construing this subsection was located in a CourtListener case-law search this session.

HOW THIS NOTICE DIFFERS FROM OTHER HIRING- AND SEPARATION-RELATED NOTICES
The disability-insurance and paid-family-leave notice described in this information sheet, required by Unemployment Insurance Code § 2613, is a distinct legal requirement from other notices a new employee may separately be entitled to receive around the time of hire or separation -- including a time-of-hire notice about workers' compensation rights (required by a different statute, Labor Code § 3551), a Wage Theft Prevention Act notice about pay rate and related terms (Labor Code § 2810.5), and a notice concerning unemployment compensation benefits that a different statute requires an employer to supply when an individual becomes unemployed (Unemployment Insurance Code § 1089). Each of these operates under its own statutory text, its own trigger, and its own required content. This document addresses only the hiring-triggered disability-insurance and paid-family-leave notice duty under Unemployment Insurance Code § 2613.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT
Please sign below to indicate that you have received and reviewed this information sheet.

Employee: Jordan Lee
Company: Acme, Inc.
Date: _______________
